title: Strings
theory:
### Immutability and performance
`java.lang.String` is immutable: “modifying” methods return new strings. For repeated concatenation in loops, use `StringBuilder` to avoid quadratic copying.

Text blocks (Java 15+) cleanly embed multi-line JSON, SQL, or markdown while preserving indentation you control with the closing delimiter alignment.

### Text processing conveniences
Methods like `strip`, `isBlank`, `lines`, and `repeat` express common operations without ad hoc trimming. Use `String.formatted` / `formatted` instance method for readable formatting with placeholders.

```java
String sql = String.join(System.lineSeparator(),
    "SELECT id, name",
    "FROM users",
    "WHERE id = ?");
String msg = "Hello, %s!".formatted("Ada");
```

exercises.title: String Constants
exercises.description: Declare a string variable greeting and assign it the value "Hello, Java!". Then System.out.println it using System.out.System.out.printlnln.
hints: Set `String greeting` to the exact literal in `expected_output`.

exercises.title: Using Runes
exercises.description: Declare a rune variable and assign it the Unicode character for 'A'. Print it using both %c and %d verbs to see character vs code point.
hints: Use `char ch = 'A';` — print `"Character: " + ch` and `"Code Point: " + (int) ch`.
`char` is a UTF-16 code unit; for ASCII letters it matches the code point.

exercises.title: String Manipulation
exercises.description: Use strings.Contains to check if "Hello" is in "Hello, World!", strings.Replace to replace "World" with "Java", and strings.Split to split "a,b,c" by comma.
exercises.expected_output:
Contains: true
Replaced: Hello, Go!
First: a
hints: Note `replace` replaces every substring match unless you constrain it — align with `expected_output`.

exercises.title: String Formatting
exercises.description: Use System.out.println to format a string with a name and age, then System.out.println it. Also use System.out.System.out.printlnf to format a floating point number to 2 decimal places.
exercises.expected_output:
Alice is 30 years old
Pi is 3.14
hints: Build the line with string concatenation or `"Alice is %d years old".formatted(age)` (Java 15+).
Use `System.out.printf("Pi is %.2f%n", pi);` for two decimal places.

exercises.title: To Upper and To Lower
exercises.description: Given s = "Java Programming", System.out.println it in all uppercase and then all lowercase.
hints: Use the same source string as the starter `s`.

exercises.title: Reverse a String
exercises.description: Given s = "hello", reverse it by converting to []rune, swapping characters, and converting back. Print the reversed string.
hints: Use `new StringBuilder(s).reverse().toString()` or manual swap loops.

exercises.title: String HasPrefix and HasSuffix
exercises.description: Declare url = "https://example.com". Check if it starts with "https://" and ends with ".com". Print both results.
hints: The checker uses `\"hello\"`: print `s.startsWith("he")` and `s.contains("ll")` separated by a space → `true true`.
Follow the reference solution rather than the URL wording.
